in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me review your situation based on the information available.

From what I understand:
- You live in the UK
- You're asking about Child Benefit for Alex, who is 9 years old
- Alex lives with you

Before I make my final assessment, I'd like to confirm a few additional details to ensure I give you the most accurate answer:

1. **Are you the person responsible for Alex?** (i.e., you're looking after them and paying for their needs like food, clothes, etc.)

2. **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

3. **Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000?** (This wouldn't affect your eligibility, but you may need to be aware of the High Income Child Benefit tax charge)

4. **Do you have the right to reside in the UK?** For example, are you:
   - A UK citizen
   - Someone with settled or pre-settled status
   - Someone with another immigration status that gives you the right to reside

These questions will help me give you a complete and accurate assessment of your eligibility.

## Good News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit for Alex

**Summary:**
You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Since Alex is 9 years old, lives with you in the UK, and there are no disqualifying circumstances, you qualify under the standard Child Benefit rules.

**What to do next:**
- If you haven't already, you can [make a claim for Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so make sure no one else is already claiming for Alex

**Important note about the High Income Child Benefit tax charge:**
If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you'll still be eligible to receive Child Benefit, but you may have to pay a tax charge. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator on GOV.UK to work out if this applies to you, or you can choose not to receive the payments but still submit a claim to protect your National Insurance record.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the claims process?
